facts.text: Bier’s name probably comes from early German settlers, perhaps a family surname, though the exact origin remains unclear.
In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Bier’s economy focused on brickmaking, using local clay from Helderberg limestone deposits.
The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad, Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, and Cumberland and Pennsylvania Railroad once ferried Bier’s bricks to national markets.
Bier sits at 39°33′18″N 78°52′10″W, 774 feet above sea level, in the Ridge‑and‑Valley province of the Appalachians.
The area averages about 39 inches of precipitation each year, with roughly 34 inches of snow, giving it a fairly even seasonal climate.
Bier was part of Frederick County until Allegany County formed in 1789, after which organized land grants encouraged farming and frontier outposts.
